STAGE 9 root cause: conexao_get_provider_categories() issued a secondary get_posts() that was NOT widened for the B2 course_provider post type, so Polylang narrowed it to English, it matched zero PT providers and /en/cursos/ rendered NO filter bar. The helper now goes through the shared conexao_b2_widen_query_args() boundary (lang => en,pt on an EN request), exactly as the events filter helpers already do. The five expected provider categories are discovered and every link stays under /en/cursos/. No EN course_provider record and no taxonomy term was created.

_provider_category is free-text post meta, not a taxonomy, so there is no linked EN term to resolve. conexao_provider_category_label() supplies the English PRESENTATION value only: it never writes English into the PT meta, never creates a term, and returns an unknown value unchanged. The canonical Portuguese 'name' and 'slug' used by the ?categoria= meta_query are untouched, so filter URLs are identical in both languages.

Selecting a category on /en/cursos/ filters the result set and stays in EN: the language is not flipped, the active state is marked, and the cards render English labels. The filter matches the same _provider_category meta value as /cursos/, so PT and EN select the identical record set.

An unknown category slug on the English archive produces zero results instead of misleading content, matching the pre-existing PT rule (the slug resolves to a sentinel meta value). Proves the EN widening did not make the filter permissive.

PT immutability at the render level: on a PT request conexao_provider_category_label() returns the stored Portuguese value verbatim, so the Portuguese archive and its filter bar are byte-identical before and after the change (same SHA-256 in the evidence).
